title: Root Edit approval requires 10% supply turnout and a majority of votes cast excluding abstentions
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 sets the Root Edit poll parameters: the Snapshot poll is "open for three (3) days," and "must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved."

The two thresholds use different denominators, and that asymmetry is the substantive design. Quorum is measured against circulating supply and counts *participation*; the majority is measured against votes cast with abstentions removed. An abstention therefore contributes to quorum while being neutral on the merits.

The consequence is that abstention is a meaningful third option rather than a wasted vote. A large holder who does not want to decide a question can still enable the electorate to decide it, and conversely a bloc wanting to defeat a proposal cannot do so by staying home if others reach 10% — it must vote against.

The short 3-day window is the counterweight to the low 10% bar: little time to organize turnout, so proposals depend on pre-existing attention generated during the Forum and Facilitator-review stages that precede the poll.
description: Abstentions count toward the participation bar but not the majority, so abstaining is an active move that helps a proposal clear quorum without supporting it.
